newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-HERTHA BERLIN LET VICTORY SLIP FROM GRASP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HERTHA BERLIN LET VICTORY SLIP FROM GRASP.

text.p: Borussia Moenchengladbach scored two late goals in the final 11 minutes on Sunday to deny Hertha Berlin their first win since promotion to the Bundesliga this season.
A huge home crowd of 52,321 had turned out at Berlin's Olympic Stadium for the match but they had to settle for a 2-2 draw as the hosts were caught off guard.
Hertha, now bottom of the league table after three matches, were 2-0 up with goals in the 32nd and 68th minutes when Moenchengladbach replied.
Peter Wynhoff scored in the 79th minute and Stefan Effenberg hit the equaliser from a free kick in the 89th.
"We know what we did wrong in the first half, we played very poorly at the start," said Effenberg. "The second half shows what we are capable of."
It was Berlin's second draw in three matches and the third straight draw for Moenchengladbach.
Karlsruhe, 3-1 winners at home to Arminia Bielefeld on Saturday, lead the Bundesliga standings after three matches level on points with Kaiserslautern.
